questions.question: You want a free public chatbot to help rewrite a client email that includes the client's PAN and portfolio value. What should you do?
options: Paste it as is; chatbots don't store data
Anonymise it or use a company-approved tool, following company data policy
Paste it but ask the chatbot to forget it afterwards
Remove only the client's first name
questions.explanation: Identity numbers and client data must not go into unapproved tools; anonymise or use an approved tool per policy.

questions.question: Which is the recommended way to handle questions about how the DPDP Act 2023 applies to a new AI workflow?
options: Interpret the Act yourself from a summary
Ask the AI model for a legal opinion and follow it
Assume it doesn't apply to internal tools
Follow company policy and consult the compliance or data protection team
questions.explanation: The lesson gives only a high-level overview; employees should rely on company policy and compliance, not their own legal interpretation.

questions.question: What is a counterfactual pair test for bias?
options: Running the same input twice and comparing outputs
Asking two different models the same question
Changing only a sensitive attribute, such as the name or city, and checking whether the output changes
Comparing English and Hindi versions of a prompt
questions.explanation: If swapping only an irrelevant attribute changes the assessment, the process may be biased.

questions.question: An AI draft of a marketing message says a product gives "safe, assured 15% returns". What is the right action?
options: Route it through compliance review instead of sending it
Send it, since the AI wrote it
Ask the AI whether it is compliant and send if it says yes
questions.explanation: Financial claims are regulated; overclaiming language must go through human compliance approval, and you remain accountable.
